newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to probe aid to German machine tools company.
newsitem.headline: EU to probe aid to German machine tools company.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was opening a probe into financial aid the German government plans to give machine tools company Doerries Scharmann GmbH.
The European Union executive said it had several doubts about the plan, including its link to a separate Commission investigation into misuse of state aid by bankrupt German shipyard Bremer Vulkan.

However, it said it had approved a separate aid plan for German machine tools company UNION Werkzeugmaschinen GmbH, formerly owned by Bremer Vulkan, along with schemes for Spanish mining company Almagrera SA and Italian metals company Enirisorse.

German authorities propose to provide Doerries Scharmann GmbH -- set up following the bankruptcy of Doerries Scharmann AG -- a state guarantee to help the company restructure and meet liquidity problems.
The Commission said last November it believed the bankrupt company, a former Bremer Vulkan subsidiary, was among the main recipients of illegally diverted state aid granted to the shipyard.
It said the aid plan for the new company did not comply with EU state aid guidelines since authorities had not submitted a proper restructuring plan.
"Furthermore, the Commission has doubts about the viability of the company in question," it said.

The Commission said it also needed to determine whether the new company was just a new version of the Bremer Vulkan subsidiary. The Commission is investigating the shipyard on charges of diverting state aid that had been approved by the Commission to restructure shipyards in eastern Germany.
The Commission said, however, that German government plans to offer UNION Werkzeugmaschinen GmbH 9.6 million marks ($5.6 million) in restructuring aid met EU requirements.

-- A Spanish government plan to prepare state-owned Almagrera to be sold to Irish private company Navan Resources by providing about 41 million ecus ($46 million) in liability write-offs and cash injections. The Commission said it believed the restructuring plan would restore the company's viability.

-- A scheme under which state-controlled energy company ENI provided 1.8 trillion lire ($1 billion) in capital injections to its metals subsidiary Enirisorse from 1992-1996 as part of a restructuing and privatisation plan.
